messages.subject: RE: Running Canopy Error
parts:
Hi Gryte,

 

For the Y matrix, you need to include the first column as ‘non-cna’. From your input, I guess you have 4 heterozygous SNAs and 1 heterozygous deletion that don’t overlap and thus the Y matrix should have two columns, where the first column are all ones and the second all zeros. Also Canopy needs the input matrix to have SNA and CNA names. I modified a bit of the code you sent – see below.

 

projectname='debug'

R <- as.matrix(read.csv('example.A'))

X <- as.matrix(read.csv('example.D'))

WM <- as.matrix(read.csv('example.WMaj'))

Wm <- as.matrix(read.csv('example.WMin'))

Y <- as.matrix(read.csv('example.Y'))

 

Y <- cbind(non_cna=rep(1,4),cna1=rep(0,4))

rownames(Y)=rownames(R)=rownames(X)=paste('sna',1:4,sep='')

rownames(WM)=rownames(Wm)='cna1'

 

C <- NULL

epsilonM <- 0.02

epsilonm <- 0.02

 

For this toy example you come up with, the most likely tree with penalty should be two branch where the SNAs and CNA on the right split from the node. This is a very simple case. Canopy currently runs iterations from 3 clones or above so it splits the cancer clone into two.

 

Feel free to let me know if you have more questions,

Yuchao
